field.name: Node name
help.type: Picks which proxy protocol this node speaks; the fields below switch automatically with it.
help.sni: The domain sent during the TLS handshake; can differ from the server address, e.g. to front through a CDN.
help.skip-cert-verify: Skips the server's certificate check, giving up MITM protection — only turn this on briefly for something like self-signed-certificate debugging.
help.plugin: Name of the Shadowsocks obfuscation plugin, e.g. obfs, v2ray-plugin, shadow-tls.
help.plugin-opts: The plugin's own options; the exact fields vary by plugin, so this is edited as raw key/value pairs.
help.network: The transport wrapper layered on top of TLS, e.g. ws (WebSocket) or grpc. Leave empty for plain TCP + TLS.
help.flow: The XTLS flow control mode, e.g. xtls-rprx-vision; leave empty when not using XTLS.
help.reality-opts: REALITY disguises the TLS handshake as a real website's; the server side must be configured to match — the public key and short ID both come from whatever the server side generated.
help.up-down: Manually pins the bandwidth to use a policy other than BBR congestion control; leave empty or 0 to use BBR. Defaults to Mbps when no unit is given.
help.token: TUICv4's legacy authentication method; it's either this or uuid + password (TUICv5), never both at once.
help.private-key: This device's own WireGuard private key — take care not to mix it up with the public key or a pre-shared key; all three are Base64-encoded but serve different purposes.
